methodNote: Rhee-era unresolved questions remain in HISTORY_DEBT/open leads and no longer block chronological advance. The Second Republic is modeled as a dual-centered parliamentary system: President Yun Po-sun is the chronological presidential backbone, while Prime Minister Chang Myon is an independent executive-center politician node.

verifiedFindings.claim: After Rhee's resignation, Foreign Minister Huh Chung became Acting President under the then succession arrangement and headed the caretaker transition.

The constitutional amendment adopted 208-3 established a bicameral legislature and cabinet system; Huh Chung became Prime Minister and Assembly Speaker Kwak Sang-hun concurrently served as Acting President pending elections.
The Fifth House of Representatives and first House of Councillors elections were held; NIKH records 175 of 233 House seats for the Democratic Party.
The joint legislature elected Yun Po-sun president 208-51; Yun first nominated Kim Do-yon for prime minister, who lost 112-111, then nominated Chang Myon, confirmed 117-107.

Democratic Party old/new faction conflict shaped cabinet formation; Chang's initial 14-member cabinet allotted only two positions to the old faction, followed by revisions adding old-faction ministers.

The Second Republic created post-April accountability legislation, including the temporary handling law for democratic-traitor criminal cases and Law No.586 punishing March 15 election-related wrongdoing.
sources: Official Gazette No.2750 / NIKH constitutional DB

verifiedFindings.claim: The Chang government pursued a national construction/public works program and a five-year economic development draft; the development-plan lineage predates the May 16 coup and also has First Republic antecedents.
sources: NIKH/National Institute of Korean History study on Second Republic economic policy

verifiedFindings.claim: The government faced organized opposition to the Korea-US economic agreement and a unanimous Assembly resolution seeking an early status-of-forces agreement; these are separate foreign-policy and domestic-mobilization event chains.
sources: NIKH study on April Revolution/innovation forces

verifiedFindings.claim: US intelligence reported coup planning by Park Chung Hee before May 16; the same record says Chang Myon was aware of coup rumors by April 26 but assessed them as not dangerous.

The May 16 military coup seized key state facilities under forces led by Park Chung Hee; contemporary US records initially described Chang Myon's government as the lawful constitutional government. On May 18 the Chang cabinet resigned and the transition to military rule accelerated.

adversarialChecks: Do not treat Yun Po-sun as the sole executive center merely because he was president under a parliamentary constitution.
Do not treat Chang Myon as powerless merely because the presidency remained visible; recover formal cabinet powers and actual decisions.
Test whether Democratic Party factional conflict alone explains governmental instability against economic, protest, military, and institutional evidence.
Test claims that the Second Republic had no economic-development plan against Construction Ministry plan records and First Republic antecedents.
Separate continuity from appropriation when comparing Second Republic and post-coup five-year plans.
Test whether Chang Myon had no coup warning against April 21-26 CIA reports, while distinguishing rumor awareness from actionable intelligence.
Do not infer Chang Do-yong's voluntary leadership from coup broadcasts using his name; contemporary US military reporting questioned authorization.
Do not infer complete Yun Po-sun support for the coup from later outcomes; reconstruct May 16-18 actions chronologically.
Separate US initial support for the lawful government from subsequent recognition/working relations with the military regime.
Separate post-April accountability legislation from individual guilt; preserve prosecution, judgment, appeal, and later findings independently.
